dates.display: 1623–1641 (senior branch in the founders' network across John's emigration decade)

incoming.explanation: The 1627 letter documents the senior branch's Court-of-Wards channel to Winthrop and Downing on which the finding rests.
The WARD 7 / C 142 inquisitions establish the wardship that put the minor heir's household under Court of Wards administration in the emigration decade.
Muskett grounds the Gurdon–Sedley–Lewkenor puritan matrix from which the letter was written.
The network is context around the senior branch, not a connection to John; the origin question is held to the identity work.
The open question presupposes the senior branch's documented position inside the founders' Court of Wards circle.

The Winthrop family's personal memorial of Martha (Lewkenor) Gurney's parents in 1605 shows the senior branch's Denham kin standing inside the Winthrops' own circle a generation before the 1627 letter, deepening the documented tie between the branch and the Massachusetts founders.
The Bracketts' compiled Sudbury origin echoes, at compiled level, the same Gurdon patronage geography documented for the senior West Barsham Gurney branch.

shortLabel: The senior West Barsham branch inside the founders' Court-of-Wards network, 1623–1641
statement: In John Gurney's emigration decade the senior West Barsham branch of the Gurney family stood inside the personal network of the Massachusetts Bay founding leadership: after Thomas Gurney III died in his father's lifetime (c.1621×1623), his son Edward Gournay succeeded Henry G15 in 1623 as a minor ward, and Edward's widowed mother worked — through the leading Suffolk puritan patron Brampton Gurdon — to John Winthrop and Emmanuel Downing at the Court of Wards, out of a Sedley/Lewkenor matrix rooted at Emmanuel College. This is a new English-side record class contemporaneous with the emigration; it makes a Norfolk Gurney's arrival in Winthrop's colony network-consistent, without itself supplying the arrival.
